# Third-party notices and license inventory

This inventory records the third-party components and locked WebUI dependency graph reviewed on 2026-10-14. It is an attribution inventory, not legal advice, a license-compatibility opinion, or public-release clearance. The Ooz native library has been rebuilt successfully from its pinned source. The current portable character build does not include FBX export, Autodesk SDK, or FMOD bindings. The corresponding-source kit excludes extracted game source, game shader/resource payloads, and `CNKeys.json`; the existing default VFS key constant is an explicitly approved inclusion exception recorded in the source manifest, with its value omitted from this notice. Verify the final archive's exact file inventory and dependency graph before distribution.

The project MIT grant is limited to original project software material that its contributors can license. It does not relicense upstream source, third-party patches, game content, user-generated files, or the components below. Preserve each component's listed license and notices. The exact texts copied for this inventory are in [`licenses/`](licenses/).

The audited NuGet set also included other native assets. Their package-level license expressions are represented above, but the audit did not establish a complete file-by-file notice map for every embedded native library. An earlier archived candidate included `AnimeStudio.FBXNative.dll`; its SDK terms/provenance and same-process combination with Ooz were not cleared. That finding applies to the earlier archive only. The current portable source/build closure excludes FBXNative, FBXWrapper, Autodesk SDK content, and FMOD bindings. The Autodesk EULA and SDK installer/evidence are intentionally not copied into this repository or the source kit. This narrower source inventory does not retroactively clear the earlier archive or establish legal clearance for a rebuilt release.

## Remaining distribution checks

- The pinned corresponding-source trees and Ooz build were validated during local build work. Each user archive must identify its matching corresponding-source archive and hash in `RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`; distribute both together, retain the listed notices, and verify both inventories. This notice alone does not establish complete GPL Ooz, AGPL Ruri, or LGPL FLAKE compliance.
- The SPIRV-Cross NuGet package declares Apache-2.0 and the package contains Apache license terms; the Windows DLL has no copyright strings or version-resource copyright metadata. Its nuspec records source commit `94605142f7b7bd6e69c9201e8e721d245c69eb7e`, which does not resolve in the named Khronos repository. Upstream SPIRV-Cross source has per-file copyright headers (including Arm Limited and individual contributors), but without a resolvable package source revision this inventory cannot claim a complete binary-specific copyright set. Keep the package-level attribution and Apache text; close this narrow provenance gap if exact native-file attribution is required for the final release.
- The Autodesk license/EULA conditions and precise binary provenance remain unresolved for the earlier archived candidate that included `AnimeStudio.FBXNative.dll`. That candidate is distinct from the current portable source/build closure; no Autodesk materials are included in this source kit.
- This inventory is not a notice map for Python packages downloaded during first-run setup or npm development/build-only dependencies, because the audited candidate did not bundle those dependencies. If either group is packaged later, extend the manifest and collect its exact license/NOTICE texts.
